definition: A term referring to the most advanced, highest-capability AI models available at a given point in time, typically large foundation models pushing the boundary of what AI systems can do.
details: Frontier models are often subject to additional safety testing and evaluation given their novel and less well-understood capabilities compared to smaller, more established models.
story: Imagine a factory floor where each workstation can glance at every other workstation before doing its part. It is the blueprint that makes everything else possible. At the bottom of every machine is a design — the shape of it, and how its pieces talk to each other. Structure decides what the model can even express — the blueprint before the bricks. That blueprint is Frontier Model.
